sentences.text: Appearance:
Mr. Gourav Shrivastava - Advocate for the petitioner  Mr. Romil Verma appearing on behalf of Advocate Gene  Mr. Akshat Yadav, learned counsel for the respondent  ORDER 1.
Heard with the aid of case diary.

2. This is first bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (now section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) for grant of bail to the applicant, who is in custody in connection with Crime No.160/2022, registered at police station Kanad, District Agar Malwa, for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 120-B, 368, 376(2)(K), 376(2)(n), 376(2)(J) of the IPC and under Section 3/4, 5l/6 J of the POCSO Act.
3. Prosecution story in brief is that at the time of incident the prosecutrix was minor around 16 years and 7 month of age.

Prior to the incident the prosecutrix and the applicant knew to the each other,
both of them like each other.

On 11/05/2022, prosecutrix went to village Ladvan to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35482 2 MCRC-53070-2024 attend a marriage and she called the co-accused Sonu, co-accused Sonu came there, thereafter both of them went to Indore by motorcycle, Sonu took the prosecutrix to his house, thereafter, present applicant and co-accused persons Shankarlal, Rambabu and Sonu took the prosecutrix to Kota, on 05.11.2024 she recovered by police meanwhile the co-accused Sonu committed upon her repeatedly.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicants have not committed the offence and have falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that the applicants have not provided shelter to the co-accused Sonu.
It is further submitted that the applicants are close relative of the co- accused Sonu, therefore, they have been implicated in the case.
It is further submitted that the applicants are lady and they are in custody since 04.12/2024.
Investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
The conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, they have no criminal antecedents, therefore, it is prayed that the applicants be released on bail.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent / State as well as learned counsel for the father of the prosecutrix opposed the prayer for grant of bail and prayed for rejection of the application.
6. Learned counsel for the objector / mother of prosecutrix pleaded that she has no objection if the applicant is granted bail.

7. Having considered the rival contentions of the learned counsels for the parties, perused the case diary, also looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and allegations made against the applicant, this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35482 3 MCRC-53070-2024 court is of considered view that this is a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Hence, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, this application is allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant - Asha Bai, Radha Bai and Tanisha be released on bail upon their furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- each with a solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for their appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (now Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023).
9.
M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
C.c. as per rules.
(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE patil/a
